# Maximum Population Year. The expected result is a year, not a count.

@example Two people are alive from 1980 to 1984. In 1985 the first one is gone and the third is born, so the count stays at 2, and 1980 is the first year with it.
[[1971,1985],[1980,1990],[1985,2001]]
=> 1980

@example Two people are alive in 1962 and 1963, and two again from 2012 to 2014; the earlier peak wins.
[[2010,2015],[1960,1964],[2012,2020],[1962,1970]]
=> 1962

@example The first person no longer counts in 2005, the year the second is born, so no year has more than one person.
[[1999,2005],[2005,2008]]
=> 1999

# One person: the answer is the year of birth.
[[1950,2050]]
=> 1950

# Born in the last possible year.
[[2049,2050]]
=> 2049

# The peak is in 2049, and 2050 is a death year: a table of 100 years
# counted from 1950 has no room for it.
[[1950,2050],[2049,2050],[2049,2050]]
=> 2049

# Counting the year of death would put two people in 1960, and 1960 would
# win; really only 1965 to 1969 have two.
[[1950,1960],[1960,1970],[1965,1975]]
=> 1965

# A death and a birth in 1990: counting the birth before the death would
# reach 2 in 1990, which no year really has.
[[1990,2000],[1980,1990]]
=> 1980

# Three separate peaks of 2, in 1952, 1993 and 2031; the earliest comes
# from the last rows.
[[2030,2032],[2031,2040],[1990,1995],[1993,1994],[1951,1953],[1952,1954]]
=> 1952

# The peak of 4 is inside a long life, well after the first birth.
[[1950,2050],[1999,2001],[2000,2003],[2000,2001]]
=> 2000

# Three people are born in 1970, but the peak of 4 is in 1983, a year with
# a single birth.
[[1970,1971],[1970,1971],[1970,1971],[1980,1990],[1981,1990],[1982,1990],[1983,1990]]
=> 1983

# Equal rows each count: three people in 1978.
[[1977,1979],[1978,1980],[1977,1979]]
=> 1978

# Lives of one year each, every one ending as the next begins.
[[2002,2003],[2001,2002],[2000,2001]]
=> 2000

# 100 people, born in each year from 2049 down to 1950 and all dying in
# 2050: the population grows every year and reaches 100 in 2049.
[[2049,2050],[2048,2050],[2047,2050],[2046,2050],[2045,2050],[2044,2050],[2043,2050],[2042,2050],[2041,2050],[2040,2050],[2039,2050],[2038,2050],[2037,2050],[2036,2050],[2035,2050],[2034,2050],[2033,2050],[2032,2050],[2031,2050],[2030,2050],[2029,2050],[2028,2050],[2027,2050],[2026,2050],[2025,2050],[2024,2050],[2023,2050],[2022,2050],[2021,2050],[2020,2050],[2019,2050],[2018,2050],[2017,2050],[2016,2050],[2015,2050],[2014,2050],[2013,2050],[2012,2050],[2011,2050],[2010,2050],[2009,2050],[2008,2050],[2007,2050],[2006,2050],[2005,2050],[2004,2050],[2003,2050],[2002,2050],[2001,2050],[2000,2050],[1999,2050],[1998,2050],[1997,2050],[1996,2050],[1995,2050],[1994,2050],[1993,2050],[1992,2050],[1991,2050],[1990,2050],[1989,2050],[1988,2050],[1987,2050],[1986,2050],[1985,2050],[1984,2050],[1983,2050],[1982,2050],[1981,2050],[1980,2050],[1979,2050],[1978,2050],[1977,2050],[1976,2050],[1975,2050],[1974,2050],[1973,2050],[1972,2050],[1971,2050],[1970,2050],[1969,2050],[1968,2050],[1967,2050],[1966,2050],[1965,2050],[1964,2050],[1963,2050],[1962,2050],[1961,2050],[1960,2050],[1959,2050],[1958,2050],[1957,2050],[1956,2050],[1955,2050],[1954,2050],[1953,2050],[1952,2050],[1951,2050],[1950,2050]]
=> 2049

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[[1952,1957],[1957,1958],[1957,1958],[1952,1956],[1952,1956],[1957,1958],[1957,1958]]
=> 1957

@gen 2 small
[[1952,1957],[1950,1953],[1955,1956],[1950,1955],[1953,1958]]
=> 1952

@gen 3 small
[[1951,1952],[1950,1956],[1956,1957],[1955,1956],[1956,1957],[1952,1957],[1950,1952],[1956,1957]]
=> 1956

@gen 4 small
[[2042,2049],[2047,2048],[2048,2050],[2044,2045]]
=> 2044

@gen 5 small
[[2049,2050],[2048,2050],[2047,2048],[2048,2050],[2048,2050],[2048,2050]]
=> 2049

@gen 6 small
[[2029,2031],[2029,2031]]
=> 2029

@gen 7 small
[[2038,2047],[2046,2047],[2046,2047],[2046,2047],[2039,2044],[2044,2045]]
=> 2046

# Full size: 100 people; lives anywhere, chains of lives each starting
# as the one before ends, and groups whose peaks tie.
@gen 2
